Dataset and baseline results for curved-surface 2D code detection under industrial lighting conditions (2026, preprint, arXiv (cs.CV)).
Authors: Milena Stojanović (outside co-author); Tomáš Novotný (outside co-author); Ksenija Ranković (R0602); Darija Pejić (outside co-author).
Keywords: dataset; 2D code detection; QR code; DataMatrix; curved surface; industrial imaging.
Publicly available datasets for 2D code (QR and DataMatrix) detection on curved surfaces are scarce, and those that exist rarely include the range of industrial lighting conditions encountered in practice. This preprint describes a dataset of 11 400 images collected on cylindrical, conical and saddle-shaped surfaces under eight distinct lighting configurations, including high-pressure sodium emulation, LED ring, telecentric backlight and mixed ambient. Images were captured at three conveyor speeds (0, 0.6 and 1.1 m/s) with two camera models. Each image is annotated with code location polygons, surface curvature class, lighting type and belt speed. Baseline detection results are reported for four open-source pipelines. ZXing-C++ achieved the highest overall decode rate of 81.3%, dropping to 64.7% on saddle surfaces. The dataset is released under a CC BY 4.0 licence and is intended to support reproducible comparison of detection methods in this under-studied setting.

[SYN-PAT-048] patent · Method and apparatus for projective surface rectification of cylindrical container barcodes in motion · 2021 · researchers R0602
Method and apparatus for projective surface rectification of cylindrical container barcodes in motion (2021, granted).
Inventors: Ksenija Ranković (R0602).
A machine vision method for decoding linear barcodes on moving cylindrical containers by estimating the visible arc width from a single camera frame, applying a piece-wise projective rectification to map the curved label region to a planar image, and then decoding with a standard 1D barcode engine. The method operates without prior knowledge of container diameter by deriving a radius estimate from the detected silhouette edges. It is suitable for implementation on industrial PCs and ARM-class embedded controllers at conveyor speeds up to 1.5 m/s. Filed with the Intellectual Property Office of the Republic of Serbia; national application number retained by the University of Novi Sad.

Authors: Miroslav Tešić (outside co-author); Ksenija Ranković (R0602); Lucia Ferrarini (outside co-author).
Keywords: barcode localisation; cylindrical surface; projective rectification; adaptive thresholding; GigE camera.

Adversarial domain adaptation for bridge railing damage detection across camera models (2019, conference, Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Machine Learning and Vision).
Authors: Rastko Ilić (outside co-author); Zoltán Fekete (outside co-author); Claudia Stănescu (outside co-author); Lidija Lukić (R0406).
Keywords: adversarial adaptation; domain alignment; bridge inspection; ResNet; camera shift.
Domain shift caused by differences between camera sensor models is a practical obstacle in deploying visual inspection systems across heterogeneous inspection fleets. This paper applies a gradient-reversal adversarial domain adaptation framework to bridge railing damage detection, where source images were collected with a Canon industrial camera and target images with a Sony mirrorless device. The backbone is a ResNet-50 fine-tuned on 4,800 source images covering four damage classes; the target domain contains 320 unlabelled and 80 labelled images. Adversarial alignment of intermediate feature maps at the third residual block reduces target-domain classification error from 31.4 % to 18.7 % relative to standard fine-tuning without adaptation. Ablations isolate the contribution of the domain discriminator at different feature resolutions.

the terms agreed up front.

Free text may propose new work and new data ("collect", "label", "set up", "measure", "aim for"), and may reason from the
claims. List a sentence only when it:
- presents as already true a fact about the company or the researcher (data, recordings, a dataset size, history,

- works on data the company is not shown to have: for every archive, dataset, log, set of past scans or recordings the

- contradicts a claim or a source;
- plans work that breaks a limit the company states (a rate it may not go below, hardware it cannot change).
Quote each such sentence whole, exactly as written. Give one reason per sentence and name the claim or source it rests on.
Return an empty list when the free text is fine.
